Output of `forgecycle help <command>` for ForgeCycle 0.6.0.

## forgecycle init

Set a project up: its configuration and the agent skill.

```text
Usage: forgecycle init [--check | --force]
       forgecycle init config [--check | --force]
       forgecycle init skill [--force]

Set a project up: its configuration and the agent skill.

Arguments:
  config      Only create, replace, or check the configuration
  skill       Only install the agent skill

Options:
  --check     Validate the configuration and change nothing; a bare init then
              checks only the configuration
  --force     Back up and replace an existing configuration, and replace a
              differing skill copy (local edits are lost)
  -h, --help  Show this help

A bare init runs init config, then init skill.

init config creates .forgecycle/config.json and appends ForgeCycle's runtime
paths to .gitignore. It refuses with exit 65 when a configuration exists.

init skill installs the agent skill this binary carries, matching its version,
into .claude/skills/forgecycle (Claude Code) and .agents/skills/forgecycle
(Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity) at the repository root. A copy that already
matches is left alone. A copy that differs is kept and listed file by file, and
the command exits 65 after installing the other directory. It works whether or
not the project is configured.

See also: forgecycle help doctor
```

## forgecycle doctor

Check configuration and adapter availability.

```text
Usage: forgecycle doctor [options]

Check configuration and adapter availability.

Options:
  --ping                  Also send each candidate a billed test prompt
  --ping-timeout SECONDS  Cap each ping (default: 120); a candidate's shorter
                          timeout_seconds still applies
  -h, --help              Show this help

Run it after editing .forgecycle/config.json to catch setup problems before a
task run. Without --ping it makes no model call. It checks:
  - each policy's decompose, planning, building, and reviewing candidate lists
  - that worktree.copy_ignored files are Git-ignored and untracked
  - ForgeCycle runtime paths that are not Git-ignored (init appends them only
    when it writes the configuration)
  - instructions files not committed at HEAD, which task run worktrees will not
    contain
  - candidates on a quota cooldown

--ping sends one tiny read-only prompt to every candidate any policy uses, with
its configured model and effort, and expects the reply FORGECYCLE_PONG. It
catches bad credentials, mistyped models, rejected effort values, and exhausted
quotas before a task run. Each ping is a real, billed model call. Candidates on
a quota cooldown are skipped, and up to 4 pings run at once. A failed ping
exits 65; an answer other than FORGECYCLE_PONG is only a warning.
```

## forgecycle status

List unfinished task runs and roadmap runs.

```text
Usage: forgecycle status [--json]

List unfinished task runs and roadmap runs.

Options:
  --json      Print an array of objects for scripts (fields below)
  -h, --help  Show this help

status shows which task run holds the repository reservation, then every task
run and roadmap run that is not done or abandoned. Use it to find run IDs after
a crash or a killed terminal. It only reads and makes no model call.

Each task run shows its state, its stop kind (interrupted for an active task
run whose process is gone), its roadmap run and attempt when it has one, and
the first suggested next command. Each roadmap run shows its state, stop kind,
current task, and next command.

The --json objects have the fields kind (task_run or roadmap_run), id, state,
phase, stop_kind, stop_detail, next, next_why, next_human, holds_reservation,
pause_requested (a live run whose pause has not taken effect yet),
roadmap_run_id, roadmap_task_id, attempt, current_task, position, and tasks.

See also: forgecycle help task status, forgecycle help roadmap status
```

## forgecycle pause

Stop what is running after its current turn.

```text
Usage: forgecycle pause

Stop what is running after its current turn.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this help

pause finds what a live process advances in this repository, the task run that
holds the repository reservation or a running roadmap run, and asks it to stop
once its current Planner, Builder, or Reviewer turn ends, gates included. It
returns at once and makes no model call; the running command stops by itself.

The task run then records a pause_requested stop that resumes into the turn it
was about to start, prints its stop block, and exits 21. A roadmap run stops
with its task run, or before it starts or resumes another task run when none is
running, records pause_requested, and exits 21. --auto-resume never resumes
past a pause.

The request is the file pause-request in the run's directory under
.forgecycle/task-runs or .forgecycle/roadmap-runs; status shows it as a pending
pause. A command that starts advancing the run removes a request left over from
a process that ended first. Nothing running exits 1.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM still stops the running agent or gate at once; pause waits
for the turn.

See also: forgecycle help unpause
```

## forgecycle unpause

Cancel a pending pause, or continue what paused.

```text
Usage: forgecycle unpause [options]

Cancel a pending pause, or continue what paused.

Options:
  --planner ID   Use candidate ID as Planner for this invocation only
  --builder ID   Use candidate ID as Builder for this invocation only; not a
                 read-only candidate
  --reviewer ID  Use candidate ID as Reviewer for this invocation only
  --auto-resume  As for task resume or roadmap resume
  -h, --help     Show this help

While the current turn still runs, unpause removes the pause request and the
run carries on as if nothing happened.

Once the run has paused, unpause continues it in the foreground: a paused task
run of a roadmap run with roadmap resume, which resumes that task run first;
any other paused task run with task resume; a roadmap run paused between tasks
with roadmap resume. The options are passed on. Options given to the paused
command, such as --builder, are not stored and must be given again.

Nothing paused exits 1. task resume and roadmap resume continue a paused run
too.

See also: forgecycle help pause, forgecycle help task resume, forgecycle help
          roadmap resume
```

## forgecycle prune

Delete all task run worktrees and stored task and roadmap runs.

```text
Usage: forgecycle prune [options]

Delete all task run worktrees and stored task and roadmap runs.

Options:
  --worktrees  Delete the contents of .forgecycle/worktrees
  --runs       Delete the contents of .forgecycle/task-runs and
               .forgecycle/roadmap-runs
  --force      Skip the confirmation prompt
  -h, --help   Show this help

With neither --worktrees nor --runs, prune deletes both. Worktrees are
unregistered from Git; task run and roadmap run branches are kept.

prune lists each directory with its entry count and size, and the total size,
then asks for confirmation. Declining exits 1 and deletes nothing.

It refuses with exit 21 while a task run holds the repository reservation, and
--runs refuses while a roadmap run is running or stopped, naming it; abandon it
first.

The operation journal that serve and observe read is not touched. --runs marks
the deleted runs' open stops in the notification history as resolved (deleted).
```

## forgecycle serve

Serve the local observability dashboard for this project.

```text
Usage: forgecycle serve [options]

Serve the local observability dashboard for this project.

Options:
  --port N          Listen on port N (default: a free port)
  --listen ADDR     Bind to IP address ADDR instead of 127.0.0.1 (see below)
  --public-url URL  Offer URL (or a bare domain) to other devices in the QR
                    code and share dialog (see below)
  --no-auth         Serve without the access token: anyone who can reach the
                    dashboard can read it
  --open            Also open the URL in the default browser
  -h, --help        Show this help

serve prints a one-time URL that contains the access token (unless --no-auth).
The dashboard shows a Now summary of what needs you, what is running, and what
just finished; the planned work as a tree of plans, tasks, and agent turns,
with each agent's handoff, activity, changes, and evidence; a plan's Stats tab
with progress percentages, effort, quality, and an estimated finish; the runs
that need you; every stop and how it was resolved; the command history; and
each candidate's quality figures (as observe --summary). Opt-in browser
notifications announce each new stop while a dashboard tab is open. The
dashboard is read-only: it exposes no approval, resume, or other mutation.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops serve; an open dashboard then says forgecycle serve was
stopped. Each start makes a new access token (unless --no-auth), so after a
restart open the newly printed URL (or pass --open); a page from the previous
server shows that its session ended and reconnects once the new URL is opened.

--listen 0.0.0.0 lets browsers on other machines open the dashboard. serve then
also prints one URL per network address, a QR code of the first one (on a
terminal only), and a warning, and accepts IP addresses and this machine's
hostname as the Host. It is plain HTTP, so use it only on a trusted network.
The dashboard's header always has a share button; its dialog has a Copy button
for the entry URL with the token and shows the same QR code when serve listens
beyond loopback or names a --public-url. Anyone who scans it can read the
project, because it holds the access token. Browser notifications need the
loopback URL.

--public-url names the address other devices use, such as
https://forge.example.com behind a TLS reverse proxy, or a bare domain such as
forge.example.com, which means plain HTTP on the port serve binds. It takes a
scheme and host (and optional port) only, with no path; anything else exits 64.
serve prints it, the QR code and the share dialog offer it instead of the
network addresses, and its host passes the Host check. A reverse proxy can
reach serve on 127.0.0.1; a bare domain needs --listen as well. Over https,
browser notifications work on other devices too.

--no-auth drops the access token: every URL is the plain page, and anyone who
can reach the dashboard can read the project. serve prints a warning. The Host
check still applies, so other websites cannot read the dashboard through your
browser.

--open uses open on macOS and xdg-open on Linux. If that fails, serve prints a
warning and keeps running.
```

## forgecycle observe

Summarize candidate quality from the operation journal.

```text
Usage: forgecycle observe --summary [options]

Summarize candidate quality from the operation journal.

Options:
  --summary      Print the per-candidate summary (required)
  --workflow ID  Only count one task run or decomposition
  --json         Print the rows as JSON for scripts
  -h, --help     Show this help

For each candidate: invocations, first-pass valid handoffs, validation failures
and the most frequent failing field, repairs and repaired successes, handoffs
ForgeCycle normalized, quota cooldowns, and mean invocation duration.
```

## forgecycle update

Replace this forgecycle binary with a release.

```text
Usage: forgecycle update [--force] [vX.Y.Z]
       forgecycle update --check

Replace this forgecycle binary with a release.

Arguments:
  vX.Y.Z                   Install this release, which may be older (default:
                           the latest)

Options:
  --check                  Print the current and latest versions and change
                           nothing
  --force                  Reinstall the same version, or update while a run's
                           process is live
  -h, --help               Show this help

update downloads the release for this platform from the public
forgecycle/forgecycle-releases repository, with no credentials. It checks the
archive against the release's checksums.txt and that the new binary reports
that version, then renames it over the running binary, symlinks resolved. So a
project's ./forgecycle updates that project's pinned version, and a forgecycle
on PATH updates itself.

When the binary sits at the root of a Git repository, update then runs the new
binary's init skill, so the project's agent skill matches. A differing skill
copy is kept, as init skill describes, with a warning.

A development build (a version such as 0.4.0-3-gabc1234) refuses a bare update,
since the latest release may be older; name the release to install. The same
version is not reinstalled without --force.

update refuses with exit 21 while a live process advances a task run or roadmap
run of the binary's project or of the current directory's, because a roadmap
run starts each task run as a new process of this binary. Unfinished runs with
no live process only warn.

Releases cover darwin and linux on amd64 and arm64, and are downloaded from
  https://github.com/forgecycle/forgecycle-releases/releases

Environment:
  FORGECYCLE_RELEASES_URL  Download releases from this URL instead, a mirror
                           with the same layout
```

## forgecycle version

Print the ForgeCycle version.

```text
Usage: forgecycle version

Print the ForgeCycle version.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this help

forgecycle --version and forgecycle -V do the same.
```

## forgecycle help

Show the command overview or one command's help.

```text
Usage: forgecycle help [task | roadmap] [command]

Show the command overview or one command's help.

Arguments:
  task | roadmap  Show the task or roadmap commands, or one of them
  command         Show that command's help

Options:
  -h, --help      Show this help

forgecycle --help and forgecycle -h show the overview too. Every command also
accepts -h or --help among its arguments, for example:
  forgecycle task run --help
```
